leftEvidence.title: A deathbed exhortation remembers David’s mercy

points.label: Action and response
points.left: Mattathias calls his sons to zeal and fidelity, names ancestors as examples, says David inherited a royal throne because he was merciful, assigns leadership, and dies.
points.right: Abijam’s sins and heart are contrasted with David, while a lamp in Jerusalem is preserved for David’s sake and Uriah is named as David’s exception.

points.label: Evidence boundary
points.left: The source places David becomes one brief virtue-and-throne example inside a larger ancestral chain inside this David setting without explaining every motive, transition, or later consequence.
points.right: The source places a compact royal evaluation praises David while explicitly retaining Uriah inside this David setting without explaining every motive, transition, or later consequence.

payload.posture: 1 Maccabees 2:49–64 and 1 Kings 15:1–8 are distinct approved David Scenes in the authored “Royal, Poetic, and Prophetic Memory” movement; holding them together exposes what continues and what changes without collapsing their sources.

rightEvidence.title: Abijam is measured against David’s heart

payload.tension: 1 Maccabees 2:49–64 foregrounds David becomes one brief virtue-and-throne example inside a larger ancestral chain; 1 Kings 15:1–8 foregrounds a compact royal evaluation praises David while explicitly retaining Uriah. Their sequence does not by itself explain every change between them.
